extracted.intended_audience: SEC reporting professionals, corporate accountants and securities lawyers preparing registration statements, proxy materials and Form 8-Ks
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and what financial statements and pro forma information are required for acquisitions (including step and aggregated acquisitions) in registration statements, proxy materials and Form 8-K filings under SEC Regulation S-X and related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of acquired-business financial statements based on timing and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The conditions that require financial information related to the acquisition of a business in a registration statement depend on the timing of consummation relative to the effectiveness/mailing date and the significance of the acquisition; these conditions are summarized in tables and evaluated at the date the registrant submits the draft registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For acquisitions consummated well before the effective/mailing date, registrants may need to include audited pre-acquisition financial statements and pro forma information depending on significance. The SEC staff may decline to review registration statements that omit required FS/pro forma information at the filing date. (See Question 2.3.140 and chapter 4 for specific number/age of periods.)

rubrics_metrics.name: 75-day registration-period vs Form 8-K timing equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: A 75-calendar-day filing period for registration/proxy statements ('not more than 74 days') is treated as substantially equivalent by the SEC staff to the Form 8-K period of 'four business days plus 71 calendar days' for the purpose of evaluating whether acquired-business financial statements timely filed under Item 2.01 of Form 8-K are required in a not-yet-effective registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Form 8-K period counts four business days separately (thereby slightly extending the calendar-day count), the staff will consider the periods substantially equivalent for this specific evaluation. (FRM 2050.1 (n 1), SEC Rel 33-10786 § I.14-15)

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of separate pre-acquisition financial statements when acquired business is reflected in registrant's audited consolidated statements
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-05 permits omission of certain separate pre-acquisition audited financial statements if the acquired business has been reflected in the registrant’s audited consolidated financial statements for specified periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance sheet: separate pre-acquisition audited balance sheet not required once the most recent audited balance sheet of the registrant is filed as of a date after the acquisition. Income statement: separate pre-acquisition statements of income/operations may be omitted once the acquired business has been included in the registrant’s audited financials for nine months or a complete fiscal year, depending on significance. (See Question 2.3.160 and table: >20%–<=40% => 9 months; >40% => complete fiscal year.) If criteria not met, full number of pre-acquisition periods required (see chapter 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy materials and when acquired-business financial statements are required
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual report furnished with annual-meeting proxy materials need not include financial statements otherwise required by S-X Rule 3-05 and Rule 11-01(a); however, certain proxy solicitations that involve Item 11 or Item 12 require Reg S-X–compliant financial statements in the proxy materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule 14A requires financial statements that fully comply with Reg S-X (including S-X Rule 3-05 and pro forma under Rule 11-01(a)) when votes are solicited with respect to Item 11 (Authorization/Issuance of Securities Otherwise Than for Exchange) or Item 12 (Modification or Exchange of Securities). See Schedule 14A, Item 14 for mergers/consolidations/complex requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of acquired-business financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements of the acquired business may be incorporated by reference into a registration statement in certain circumstances (Forms S-3, F-3, and, under criteria, S-1, S-11, F-1), but they must comply fully with Reg S-X whether included directly or incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If previously filed information (e.g., in a Form 8-K or Form 10-K) is not sufficiently complete or timely to meet registration statement requirements, additional information may be required. Incorporation by reference establishes legal responsibility for the included information just as if reproduced in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of individually insignificant acquisitions for registration statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must aggregate acquisitions (and probable-to-be-acquired businesses and real estate operations since the most recent audited balance sheet) that are individually insignificant — categories include consummated acquisitions <20%, consummated acquisitions >20% but <=50% for which FS are not yet required due to the 75-day grace period, and probable acquisitions <50% — to assess aggregate significance for registration statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the aggregate impact of these acquisitions exceeds 50% significance, the registrant must provide: (1) pro forma financial information depicting the aggregate impact of these acquisitions and real estate operations, in all material respects; and (2) historical financial statements covering at least the most recent fiscal year and the most recent interim period for any acquired or probable-to-be-acquired business that is >20% significant. (S-X Rule 3-05(b)(2)(iv))

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation rules differ between registration statements and Form 8-K
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregation of unrelated acquisitions for the 50% test is required only for registration statement filings and certain proxy materials; Form 8-K requires aggregation only for related businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction means separate treatment for Form 8-K (Instruction 4 to Item 2.01) versus registration statement aggregation requirements. The legacy 'substantial majority' requirement was eliminated but aggregation for the 50% test remains for registration statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated timeline and consequences when financial statements are not available
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant cannot provide S-X Rule 3-05 financial statements in a registration statement under the 1934 Act (Forms 10 and 20-F), the SEC staff may take different actions depending on whether the filing is voluntary or nonvoluntary; inability to comply can prohibit effectiveness or delay filing until operations are included in audited consolidated results for required periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonvoluntary 1934 Act registrations (e.g., triggered by Section 12(g)), the staff will generally take no action if the registrant does not list securities or promote trading. The staff will object to effecting a deficient voluntary 1934 Act registration statement and may request withdrawal. Example: if an acquired company cannot provide FS for a 55% acquisition, the registrant may be prohibited from filing a registration statement until the acquired operations have been included in audited consolidated results for at least 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement and disclosure requirements for recently acquired subsidiary issuers and guarantors (S-X Rule 13-01/13-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a parent recently acquired a significant business and the acquired business or any of its subsidiaries are issuers or guarantors of guaranteed securities (or securities pledged as collateral), S-X Rule 13-01 (and 13-02) require pre-acquisition summarized financial information for each recently acquired subsidiary issuer or guarantor, in addition to S-X Rule 3-05 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-X Rule 13-01 allows the option to include required disclosures outside the financial statements (e.g., MD&A) on an unaudited basis. These summarized disclosures may be required on an accelerated timeline compared to audited pre-acquisition financial statements. Registrants perform the same significance tests under S-X Rule 3-05 to determine >20% significance for these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller Reporting Companies (SRCs) and Regulation A — alignment but scaled form/content
rubrics_metrics.description: SRCs follow S-X Rule 8-04 (which directs application of S-X Rule 3-05 requirements substituting S-X 8-02/8-03 where applicable); the substantive requirements for providing financial statements of acquired or probable-to-be-acquired businesses are aligned with larger registrants, though the form and content of the acquired-business statements may follow SRC-scaled rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRC-specific rules may require only two annual periods (versus three for non-SRCs) for the form/content of FS (S-X Rule 8-02), but this does not change the number of pre-acquisition periods an SRC provides for a significant acquisition (other registrants also generally provide at most two years). Regulation A issuers apply S-X Rule 8-04 and may have scaled requirements (unaudited, shorter periods, or less frequent updates in certain cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step acquisitions — when separate acquired-business financial statements or pro forma information are required
rubrics_metrics.description: A step acquisition (increase in investment in an existing subsidiary) is considered an acquisition of a business; registrants must evaluate whether S-X Rule 3-05 financial statements are required on Form 8-K and/or in a registration statement, and whether pro forma information is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, an increase in investment in a consolidated subsidiary does not require separate FS because consolidated FS include the acquired business; however, separate historical FS may be required when: (1) the registrant’s consolidated financial statements have not included the subsidiary for a sufficient period and separate FS have not been previously filed; or (2) S-X Rule 3-05 does not apply (e.g., merger proxy or Form S-4 where target FS for the same periods as an annual report must be presented). Pro forma information may be required under S-X Rule 11-01(a)(8) if material even when separate acquired-business FS are not presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma financial information requirements when acquisitions are material or aggregate >50%
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information is required to depict the effect of acquisitions when material and specifically is required to show the aggregate impact of aggregated individually insignificant acquisitions exceeding 50% significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2021 amendments expanded pro forma requirements to include aggregate effects of all acquisitions, in all material respects, to help investors understand overall effect. When aggregate >50%, pro forma must depict aggregate impact in all material respects; when an individual acquisition is >20% (but financial statements not otherwise required due to timing), pro forma and possibly historical FS for that acquisition may also be required. (See Questions 2.3.190, examples 2.3.50–2.3.60.)
